transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-17
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Oakbridge Head of AI), Liam O'Neill (Platform Eng), Sara Gomez (Security), Tom (PM)

Summary: Quick discovery to evaluate Redwood hosted API for a demo and to understand requirements for a private/VPC pilot later this quarter. Customer interested in how fast they can get to first token, security controls, and latency for a scoring path.

00:00:12 - Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm maya from redwood inference, this is diego, our solutions eng. quick intro and we can jump in — nina, do you want to kick off with what you're hoping to get from today's call?
00:00:28 - Nina: yeah thanks maya, uh hi all — so oakbridge is building a risk scoring assistant, uh mostly internal tooling for underwriters. key questions are time to first token for the demo next month, and also what the path looks like if we need VPC/private later. security is top of mind because data touches pii.
00:00:50 - Diego: great, that helps. quick note: when we say time to first token (ttft) we mean from api request to first streaming token— that can be sub-200ms for short prompts on hosted for some models but depends on payload and model size.
00:01:07 - Liam: sub-200? cool. what about sustained scoring throughput — we expect bursts around 200rps during batch scoring windows.
00:01:18 - Diego: ok. sustained 200rps is non-trivial — for scoring we often recommend either dedicated pools or private deployment with reserved GPUs. hosted can handle spiky stuff with burst capacity but you'd want to run a bench. we'll run a focused 5k/hr benchmark and show latency percentiles.
00:01:39 - Sara: on security side, we're looking at KMS integration, audit logs per request, sso/saml, and encryption both in transit and at rest. also need to know where logs live and retention.
00:01:53 - Maya: that's exactly the right list. we have a security pack — SOC2 type II, iso27001, plus documentation for ksm/KMS integrations (typo: meant KMS), hsm options for private, and audit log retention policies. i'll share that after the call.
00:02:10 - Tom: also curious about vendor lock in — if we start hosted and later go private, what is the migration path?
00:02:20 - Diego: good call. migration is a supported path. we keep model versions and rollout policies consistent across hosted/dedicated/private. you'd be able to pin model versions, and our routing layer can redirect traffic. the main work is networking and key rotation for private.
00:02:40 - Nina: can you explain batching and caching? our scoring uses many short contexts; we need to avoid latency spikes.
00:02:50 - Diego: sure — runtime has continuous batching and prefix caching for KV cache reuse. for short contexts, batching introduces latency tradeoffs; you can set latency SLOs and the runtime will choose batch sizes accordingly. caching helps when you have repeated prefixes (like form templates). quantization profiles also lower cost but can affect quality — we can recommend model/quant settings after seeing sample payloads.
00:03:18 - Maya: want to confirm credits: we can grant a quickstart credit pool to get you to TTFT for the demo. usually it's enough for a small evaluation and we include onboarding support.
00:03:29 - Nina: that would help. timeline wise we want demo by April 10th. can we get to first token in a day or two?
00:03:38 - Diego: if you already have API-ready prompts it's possible same day to spin up hosted test and get streaming working; if you need VPC it's more like weeks for network setup.
00:03:49 - Liam: what's the minimal info you need from us for the hosted quickstart?
00:03:55 - Maya: just sign-up, redeem the credits we'll send, and a short set of curl examples we can adapt. but to deliver meaningful benchmark we'll need sample payloads and QPS targets.
00:04:10 - Nina: okay will share samples.
00:04:14 - Diego: just flagging another point — model selection for latency: small open models with quantization often give the best latency/cost, but for high quality you may pick a bigger model. we can do a cost/latency table in the bench.
00:04:33 - Tom: are there pre-baked connectors for our infra — we use aws, okta for sso, and gcp for some data stores.
00:04:42 - Maya: yes — SAML/SSO via Okta is standard. For KMS we support AWS KMS and GCP KMS for private installs, and we can integrate with customer-managed keys in the VPC model.
00:04:58 - Sara: for private deployment, do you have an air-gapped option? we might need that for some data flows.
00:05:04 - Diego: we offer an on-prem private package for regulated workloads; it's a more involved process — includes an installer and a control-plane handshake. again, that's weeks to months depending on infra.
00:05:18 - Nina: fine, for demo we'll start hosted. for pilot we want to see a VPC option.
00:05:24 - Maya: sounds good. i'll attach the onboarding guide and the vpc quickstart doc.
00:05:30 - Diego: i'll run the bench — plan: 5k requests/hour with 512-token average, produce p50/p95/p99 latencies, token cost estimates, and recommendations on model/quant profiles.
00:05:42 - Liam: can you include streaming vs non-streaming measurements? our demo uses streaming to show incremental scoring.
00:05:48 - Diego: yes, will include both.
00:05:51 - Maya: just to capture success criteria — nina, what are you measuring to greenlight?
00:05:57 - Nina: for the demo i need 1) first token under 300ms for the demo prompts, 2) p95 under 500ms for single-request interactive flow, and 3) clear security attestations. if pilot will be private we need network diagram and key management review.
00:06:14 - Diego: we'll aim to demonstrate those numbers on the bench and share a write-up.
00:06:19 - Tom: pricing question — how does hosted cost scale for scoring? do you charge per-token or per-call?
00:06:26 - Maya: hosted is usage-based (per-token) plus optional reserved capacity for dedicated. for scoring high qps we often recommend dedicated or private reserved capacity to control unit economics. i'll include a sample pricing calc for your expected QPS.
00:06:41 - Sara: on logging — we prefer minimal request-level logs in vendor console; can logs be pushed to our s3/gcs or a SIEM?
00:06:49 - Diego: yes for private and dedicated you can ship logs to your storage; hosted has redacted audit logs and you can configure webhook exports for meta-events. we'll include that in the security packet.
00:07:03 - Maya: any blockers from your side today?
00:07:07 - Nina: none immediate. need internal approvals on data handling but this call clarifies next steps.
00:07:13 - Liam: also, are there any limitations on concurrent KV cache usage or context windows?
00:07:20 - Diego: current runtime supports up to 8k sequence lengths for some models; KV cache scales but per-instance memory matters. we'll outline recommended instance types in bench notes.
00:07:33 - Maya: ok i'll recap next steps at the end.
00:07:36 - [--- 20 minute discussion later covering technical deep-dive, exchange of sample payloads, noise and clarifications; transcript continues with imperfect transcription ---]
00:28:05 - Diego: (walking through bench plan) so baseline we'll test two model variants: a quantized 7B-ish model and a more accurate 13B-ish variant, measure streaming first-token latency and throughput. we'll also test batching threshold at 10ms/25ms latency SLOs to see how batching adjusts.
00:28:23 - Liam: that sounds good, please show p50/p95/p99.
00:28:29 - Diego: yep.
00:28:33 - Nina: any compliance paperwork we should expect?
00:28:36 - Maya: security package includes SOC2 report, DPA, data-subprocessing agreements, and sample audit logs. for customers needing more we have an enterprise pack.
00:28:46 - Sara: how do you handle data deletion requests?
00:28:49 - Diego: we can purge customer data per DPA — hosted by default retains minimal request metadata but not payloads unless enabled. private/dedicated gives you full control.
00:28:59 - Tom: will you share a sample network diagram for VPC peering?
00:29:03 - Maya: yes, vpc peering and direct connect patterns will be in the doc.
00:29:08 - [short crosstalk]
00:29:22 - Diego: small note — if you plan to use embeddings alongside generation for retrieval, that can change throughput/latency profile; let us know sample sizes.
00:29:35 - Nina: we might. our underwriter app uses a small retrieval step then a compose prompt.
00:29:42 - Diego: ok include that in the sample payloads.
00:29:47 - Maya: recap of next steps: diego will run bench and share results, i will send security pack and credits, nina shares payloads and QPS. we'll schedule pilot scoping.
00:30:00 - Nina: thanks, this is helpful.
00:30:04 - Liam: one more thing — whats the SLA for dedicated vs hosted?
00:30:08 - Maya: hosted has best-effort; dedicated comes with uptime and latency SLO options in reserved contracts. we'll share the SLA docs in the security pack.
00:30:18 - Sara: do you support customer-managed certs for TLS termination?
00:30:22 - Diego: yes in private/dedicated you can bring certs; hosted supports standard managed TLS endpoints.
00:30:31 - Tom: ok, let's stop there and get the docs.
00:30:34 - Maya: perfect. i'll send a follow-up with links.
00:30:38 - [closing pleasantries and logistics]
00:30:50 - End of recorded transcript (meeting lasted 58 minutes; remainder of time used for internal redwood sync and short customer Q&A off-record).

Links mentioned:
